current_activity: XII Corps attacks from the Odon bridgehead to secure the Bougy-Evrecy road before Goodwood
notes: Event date: 15 July 1944, night (Ellis, vol. I, p. 334). Event definition: On the night of 15 July the preliminary attacks begin across the front between the west of Caen and Tilly-sur-Seulles; XII Corps, starting from the Odon bridgehead, is to secure a firm base on the road south-east from Bougy through Evrecy with a view to an advance towards Aunay-sur-Odon or Thury-Harcourt; it fights hard and continuously until Goodwood begins on 18 July (p. 334). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 334: "Preliminary British operations began on the night of the 15th with attacks which extended across the whole front between the west of Caen and Tilly"; "XII Corps starting from the Odon bridgehead was first to secure a firm base on the road running south- east from Bougy through Evrecy". Location: Odon bridgehead (existing place PL0256) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the Odon bridgehead from which the corps started; the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the Odon bridgehead as the start and the Bougy-Evrecy road as the objective; no corps headquarters place is given.

current_activity: XII Corps follows the German withdrawal with the 53rd and 59th Divisions; by evening the centre is at Evrecy
notes: Event date: 4 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 408). Event definition: After Panzer Group West begins its withdrawal on the night of 3 August, XII Corps follows it closely with the 53rd and 59th Divisions, hindered by mines and booby traps; by the evening of 4 August its left is at the Orne near Amaye, its centre has reached Evrecy and its right, with XXX Corps, has occupied the ruins of Villers-Bocage (p. 408). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 408: "Its first effect was on Second Army"; "By the evening of the 4th the left was at the Orne near Amaye, the centre had reached Evrecy". Location: Evrecy, Calvados (place added in the July tranche) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Evrecy, the centre of the corps line on the evening; the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Evrecy as the place reached by the centre of the corps (p. 408).

current_activity: Sheds the 59th Division, selected for disbandment, and takes the 15th to seize a bridgehead near Louviers
notes: Event date: 24 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 453). Event definition: XII Corps has to wait for the Canadians to move, sheds the 59th Division, which is selected for disbandment, and receives the 15th Division in its place to seize the corps bridgehead near Louviers; by 24 August the corps is well on its way and its armoured cars are about to meet American patrols on the Risle south-east of Bernay (p. 453). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 453: "It had to shed the 59th Division, unhappily selected for disbandment"; "By the 24th the corps was well on its way". Location: Louviers, Eure (new place) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Louviers, the objective of the corps crossing; the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Louviers as the place of the corps bridgehead (p. 453).

current_activity: Pheasant: advance west from the Eindhoven-Nijmegen corridor begins; all calls for air support are met
notes: Event date: 22 October 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 123, 124). Event definition: XII Corps, on the left flank of the Eindhoven-Nijmegen corridor and facing west, begins its advance on 22 October as part of Second Army's strong thrust westwards on the general axis 's-Hertogenbosch-Breda; on its right are the 53rd Infantry and 7th Armoured Divisions with the 4th and 33rd Armoured Brigades and on its left the 51st and 15th Infantry Divisions and the 6th Guards Tank Brigade; the weather prevents flying until later in the day, when all calls for immediate army support are met by the Second Tactical Air Force (pp. 123-124). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 123: "a strong thrust westwards on the general axis"; p. 124: "When the advance of XII Corps began on October the 22nd the weather prevented flying but later that day visibility improved and all calls for immediate army support were met by the Second Tactical Air Force". Location: 's-Hertogenbosch, Noord-Brabant (new place), the first objective on the axis of advance with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is 's-Hertogenbosch, the first objective on the axis s'Hertogenbosch-Breda; the corps headquarters is not named and the advance began from the corridor east of the town. Location support: Ellis names 's-Hertogenbosch as the first place on the axis of the corps advance (p. 123). Context: Flagged addition: a 1944 row added in British Batch 2 only so that the new OP-PHEASANT has a British claim; the operation name and dates come from Wikipedia (R672), Ellis does not name the operation.
